purpose: Rules for tools/license_provenance_gate.py. Reuses existing policy configs by reference instead of duplicating them.

required_elements.pattern: USDOL/ETA|U\.S\. Department of Labor, Employment and Training Administration

required_when_modified.pattern: USDOL/ETA has not approved, endorsed, or tested these modifications

recommended_elements.pattern: O\*NET®? is a trademark of USDOL/ETA

required_elements.pattern: USDOL/ETA|U\.S\. Department of Labor, Employment and Training Administration

truth_boundary: Gate output is rights/provenance evidence for one asset version. It is not a listing, a price, or a production-ready claim. approved_for_sale additionally requires a complete plan 5.2 synthesis asset record (asset.json), scorecard >= standard tier minimum, and an explicit owner_approval record; without owner approval the maximum outcome is approved_for_private_use.

package_status_mapping.description: How per-asset gate outcomes roll up to the plan 5.2 package license_gate_status (pass | fail | reference_only_bundle, plus pre-gate pending). Implemented by tools/license_provenance_gate.py package_gate_status().
package_status_mapping.pending: no included assets yet, or any included asset has no license_gate.json / outcome pending
package_status_mapping.pass: every included asset outcome is approved_for_sale and excluded_reference_only_sources is empty
package_status_mapping.reference_only_bundle: every included asset outcome is approved_for_sale and at least one reference-only source is listed in excluded_reference_only_sources (cited, not shipped)
package_status_mapping.fail: any included asset outcome is approved_for_private_use, reference_only, or blocked (reference-only material must be moved to excluded_reference_only_sources, not included)

synthesis_asset_sale_requirements.description: approved_for_sale also requires a complete plan 5.2 synthesis asset record (asset.json).

holdout_verification.description: Opt-in (--verify-holdout-remote) independent verification of holdout evidence records against the canonical GitHub remote. Implemented in tools/license_provenance_gate.py (verify_holdout_remote); it never imports or runs the producer's own verifier. Without the flag (or when verification fails) an asset relying on holdout evidence is capped at approved_for_private_use (required_for_sale). With the flag, a record counts only if every check passes; any mismatch or network failure is a sale-scope gap (cap approved_for_private_use), never a rights failure.
holdout_verification.required_for_sale_note: When true, approved_for_sale is impossible while the asset relies on any holdout record (resolved, passed: true) that was not remotely verified in this run: without --verify-holdout-remote, or when verification fails, the outcome is capped at approved_for_private_use with 'holdout evidence not remotely verified; required for sale'.
holdout_verification.signer_note: Placeholders, empty until the grader registers a key. A signature is required when required_signer_fingerprints is non-empty or ssh_allowed_signers_file is set. Then grading_commit AND the commit that introduced the GRADING_FINAL.txt bytes present at grading_commit (if different) must each carry a valid signature from a listed signer, checked with git verify-commit in the sanitized git environment: OpenPGP via /usr/bin/gpg in a fresh GNUPGHOME holding only the armored keys in signer_public_keys, with the signing or primary key fingerprint (40 hex) listed in required_signer_fingerprints; SSH via /usr/bin/ssh-keygen with gpg.ssh.allowedSignersFile set to ssh_allowed_signers_file (principal must match, namespaces="git"), or to a temporary file holding only the signing key when its SHA256:... fingerprint is listed in required_signer_fingerprints. Paths are relative to this repository.
holdout_verification.expected_shas_note: Optional pins kept outside the producer's repository (e.g. our own copy of their VERIFIED_SHAS.json). expected_shas maps an evidence_id or run_id to {grading_commit, reveal_commit, remote_tip_sha}; expected_shas_file is a JSON file in VERIFIED_SHAS.json format (run_id + SHAs) or such a mapping. When a pin exists for a record, grading_commit and reveal_commit must be identical and the pinned remote_tip_sha must still be reachable from the branch tip, so a later force-push that rewrites history fails. require_expected_shas: true makes a pin mandatory.
holdout_verification.reveal_rules_note: Reveal-order rules (parity with the producer's verify_holdout at dde106b, plus two stricter ones): REVEALED_KEY.json absent at grading_commit and in every ancestor; touched by exactly one non-merge commit across ALL allowed branches (the reveal), a strict descendant of grading_commit, and never modified, removed or re-added (merges included); the revealed key's bytes never committed under any path or on any allowed branch outside grading_commit's strict descendants; grading_sheet.csv and GRADING_FINAL.txt byte-identical at every commit from grading_commit to the reveal; the record and results file unchanged after the reveal; and every results file, record and FINALIZED.txt for this key commitment, in any commit reachable from any allowed branch (deleted files included), names this grading_commit.
